Subject: RE: PixelMed — DPA redlines (initial pass)

Looping in my notes from the review:
- SCCs: technically fine to attach the Commission SCCs as-is; we prefer to keep the rest of our DPA clauses intact and reference the SCCs as an enclosure. We will not accept language that rewrites liability waterfall beyond our standard MSA limits.
- Controller/Processor: PixelMed’s proposed Exhibit A currently lists Redwood as "processor" for inference and "processor/controller" for aggregated analytics. Proposed compromise: explicitly call out processing activities and map them to roles (e.g., inference runtime = processor; analytics derived metrics = joint controller for specific telemetry datasets).
- KMS: We can support customer-managed keys for a named subset of datasets but need a scoped addendum (list of buckets/topics + SLA implications).

Action items: Karthik to verify deployment topology vs hosting_region_map.png; Laura to produce a short redline summary we can send back.

-Ben

Subject: Re: PixelMed — hosting map technical check

Checked hosting map: we can commit to US regions (us-west-2 and us-east-1) for PixelMed production with the following caveats:
- Any backup/DR replicas currently run in eu-central-1 for cross-region resiliency — we can propose a contractual carveout to keep backups in US-only or add strict encryption+access controls if PixelMed requires strict data localization.
- Customer-managed KMS: supported via our Dedicated offering (requires reserved capacity + KMS integration). For pilot on hosted plan, we can add envelope encryption but not full customer KMS segregation.
- Subprocessors: we will supply a subprocessor manifest and commit to 30 days' notice for changes.

I recommend two variants in the reply:
A) Hosted pilot path: accept encryption envelope + operational controls and a pilot addendum (faster sign).
B) Dedicated path: full KMS handoff and US-only backups (requires procurement/engineering lead time).

-Karthik

Emma / Jason — please find a short summary of our positions below and inline suggested wording in the attached PDF (redline_summary_notes.pdf). Key points:
1) SCCs: We accept attachment of the Commission SCCs but request a short clause that confirms Redwood will not be a controller for PixelMed customer data except as explicitly mapped in Exhibit A. Suggested text: "For the avoidance of doubt, Redwood is a Processor with respect to customer production data listed in Exhibit A; any additional uses are subject to separate written agreement."
2) Roles & Analytics: Proposed clause to define analytics-derived datasets as "processed metrics" with joint governance for metric definitions only (no controller-level liabilities).
3) KMS / Hosting: Offer two options (see Karthik's note). For the pilot we request PixelMed accept envelope encryption + enhanced access logs; for production Dedicated deployment we will support customer-managed KMS and US-only backups.

Next steps we propose:
- PixelMed indicates whether pilot with envelope encryption is acceptable (fastest).
- If PixelMed requires KMS in pilot, procurement signs Dedicated SOW and we set realistic timelines (6–8 weeks).

If you agree, Ben and I will send a tracked redline to your DPA document with the alternative language.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
